I. Introduction
1. On 28 April 2026, the FEI Tribunal issued a decision (the Original Decision) in which Mr.
Fahad Waleed, as the Registered Trainer of the horse, DENALI QH, FEI ID 109AP47 (the
Horse), received a suspension relating to the positive finding of Triamcinolone Acetonide
in a sample taken from the Horse at CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04.2025 (the Event).
Mr. WALEED (the Additional Person Responsible or APR) was notified of the positive
finding by the FEI and the potential penalties under Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping
& Controlled Medication Rules (the EADCMRs) on 19 May 2025. No response was
received by the FEI from the APR at the time the charge was notified nor at any time
thereafter prior to the issuance of the Original Decision on 28 April 2026 pursuant to
which MR. WALEED received a suspension for a period of six (6) months, a fine of three
thousand, five hundred Swiss Francs (CHF 3’500) and legal costs of two thousand Swiss
Francs (CHF 2’000).
2. Subsequent to the publication of the Original Decision, the FEI and the FEI Tribunal (the
Tribunal) were informed on 7 May 2026 by the APR that at the date of the sample
collection and alleged violation, he was not, in fact, the Registered Trainer of the Horse in
the FEI database.
3. Therefore, on 7 May 2026 the APR requested that this matter be reviewed and that his
position and responsibility during the relevant period be taken into consideration.
4. Applicable Rules Provisions
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List).
▪ FEI 2024 Endurance Rules, 12th Edition, effective 1 January 2024 (ERs).
5. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not otherwise
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
2

II. Factual background
6. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC-recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage and para-dressage, jumping, eventing, driving and para-driving,
endurance, and vaulting.
7. The Tribunal notes that at the time of the Original Decision, it was informed by the FEI that
the APR, a registered Trainer from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (the KSA-NF), was the
registered Trainer for the Horse, which competed with its rider Mr. Majed ALQAHTANI (the
Person Responsible or the PR) FEI ID: 10363591, at the Event. Under Article 2.1 of the
EADCMRs, a registered trainer of a horse in the discipline of Endurance in a competition is
considered an Additional Person Responsible (APR) for violations of the EADCMRs .
8. As mentioned at paragraph 1, subsequent to the issuance of the Original Decision, the
APR informed the FEI that he was not the Registered Trainer at the time of the violation.
Further to which the FEI informed the Tribunal via email on 11 May 2026 that following a
review of the information recorded in the FEI database, the FEI confirmed that Mr Waleed,
the APR, was not the Registered Trainer at the time of the sample collection.
9. As such, the Tribunal considered the facts submitted and issued an Operative Decision
on 21 May 2026 in respect of these proceedings, and set aside the Decision including the
findings and sanctions imposed on the APR.
III. Terms of the Decision
10. As a result, the FEI Tribunal Panel (the Panel) confirms the following decision originally
issued on 21 May 2026:
a) The Panel hereby sets aside the finding (dated 28 April 2026) of the violation of Article
2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”)
against Mr. Fahad WALEED (APR);
b) The Panel lifts the Suspension imposed on the APR effective immediately;
c) The Panel sets aside the fine imposed on the APR;
d) The Panel sets aside the order for costs imposed on the APR;
e) This Decision is notified to the APR, to the FEI and to Equestrian Federation of Saudi
Arabia.

text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
24 March 2026
In the matter of
Mr. Majed ALQAHTANI- (PR: Ref. C25-0039)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT21 DENALI QH)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Diane Pitts (USA)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0039 [FEI 2025/FT21 DENALI QH]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Majed ALQAHTANI/10363591/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Fahad WALEED/10306368/KSA
Event/Date: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04.2025
Event/Code: 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Triamcinolone Acetonide
Bar Code Nos.: 1417731

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Mr Majed ALQAHTANI (the
PR) committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled
Medication Rules – The Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites
or Markers in a Horse’s Sample. The FEI notified the PR of the alleged charge in his capacity
as the Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not otherwise
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. The PR is an Endurance Rider from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia who competed in the
CEI1* 100 – Riyadh (KSA), held on 24-26 April 2025 (the Event), with his horse, Denali QH
(the Horse).
5. The FEI (together with the PR, the Parties), is the sole IOC-recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage and para-dressage, jumping, eventing, driving and para-driving,
endurance, and vaulting.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 26 April 2025 at the Event. The Horse’s
sample returned a positive finding for Triamcinolone Acetonide, a Prohibited Substance
under the Equine Prohibited List.
2

7. Triamcinolone Acetonide is a corticosteroid anti-inflammatory agent used in the
treatment of orthopaedic disease. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance
under the Equine Prohibited List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 19 May 2025, the FEI informed the PR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM
Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. In the Notification Letter, the PR was informed that he had the right to request the
Horse’s B sample to be analysed. The B-Sample analysis was not requested.
10. On 21 and 25 May 20251, the PR replied to the Notification Letter and contested that the
Sampling Procedure was improperly conducted. The PR argued that he had not been
informed of the official nature of the testing, that he signed the FEI Sampling Form
without fully understanding its content, and that he did not see the Sample being placed
in a properly secured box.
11. In an email of 29 May 2025, the PR further denied the administration of any Controlled
Medication substance, supplement, or veterinary treatment containing Triamcinolone
Acetonide, or any other Prohibited Substance to the Horse, either by himself or by any
member of his team. He reiterated that the Sample Collection Procedure had been
unclear and improperly conducted, adding that he had been asked to sign the FEI
Sampling Form before the Sample was taken and without being made aware that the
Form could later be used in a disciplinary context. He added that he did not realise the
seriousness of the situation, as it was only his second FEI competition.
12. Despite various reminders from the FEI Legal Department i.e., 24 June and 25 August
2025, no further reply was submitted by the PR, nor did the PR request a hearing.
13. In accordance with Article 8.3.6 of the ECM Rules, if the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel (where applicable) does not elect the Administrative
Procedure within the fixed time limit, the Administrative Sanctions shall be considered
declined, and the case shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal for final Decision.
14. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the FEI’s
Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
1 The two emails sent on 21 and 25 May 2025 were identical in content.
3

15. On 19 December 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel (the
Panel) to decide this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the
constitution of the Panel by 7 January 2026. In addition, the PR was invited to respond to
the FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence
by 26 January 2026. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to
request a hearing by 29 January 2026, at the latest.
16. On 19 December 2025, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Panel. The PR never replied; therefore, his silence was taken as agreement to the
constitution of the Panel..
17. The PR did not file a formal submission or request a hearing despite having been notified
of the Tribunal’s letter via email directly to him and through the Saudi NF. Therefore, the
Final Decision was rendered by the Sole Panel Member based on the papers submitted
within the deadline.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:2
A. Submissions by the PR
18. The PR made no submissions other than the email submissions outlined in paragraphs
10 and 11 of this Decision.
B. Submissions by the FEI:
19. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
19.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample. As a strict
liability offence, it is not necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use
be demonstrated in order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
19.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies the
requirements of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
19.3 Article 118.3 of the GRs establishes that, “the Person Responsible shall be the
Athlete who rides […] the Horse during an Event […].” The PR is the Athlete who rode
2 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the Parties’ written submissions.
4

the Horse at the Event.
19.4 Article 9.1 of the ECM Rules establishes that an ECM Rule “in connection with a
Test in a given Competition automatically leads to the Disqualification of the result(s)
of the Person Responsible and Horse combination obtained in that Competition with
all resulting Consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and
prizes. […] Even if a Sanction is reduced or eliminated under Article 10 below, such
reduction or elimination does not reverse the automatic Disqualification of the
Result(s) mandated by this Article 9.“
19.5 Article 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules also provides that, “an ECM Rule violation occurring
during or in connection with an Event shall, upon the Decision of the FEI Tribunal,
lead to Disqualification of all of the Person Responsible's results obtained in that
Event, with any and all Horses, with all Consequences, including forfeiture of all
medals, points and prizes […].”
19.6 To maintain a level playing field, the FEI requests the disqualification of all the
results obtained by the PR and the Horse during the Event, in accordance with
Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules.
19.7 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that a Person Responsible with no previous
ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is subject to a
period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless they can rebut the presumption of
Fault on a balance of probability.
19.8 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the PR must establish to
the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the Triamcinolone
Acetonide entered the Horse’s system. The PR must also demonstrate one of the
following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Prohibited Substance. If
proven, the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article
10.5 of the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
5

19.9 The FEI submitted that the PR must provide clear and convincing evidence that
proves how the Triamcinolone Acetonide entered the Horse’s body. In his
submissions dated 21, 25 and 29 May 2025, the PR alleged that the Sample
Collection Procedure was unclear and improperly conducted. In particular, the
PR argued that: (i) he had not been informed of the official nature of the testing
nor of the procedural implications of signing the FEI Sampling Form; (ii) he had
been requested to sign the FEI Sampling Form prior to the Sample being taken;
and (iii) the full sampling protocol had not been followed in his presence, as he
was asked to leave immediately after the Sample was collected and therefore
did not witness the Sample being placed and sealed in a properly secured box.
19.10 In relation to point (i), the FEI submitted that the PR bore the legal responsibility
for the Horse, including responsibility under the GRs and Veterinary Regulations
(the VRs), and was liable under the applicable FEI Legal Regulations. It was also
the obligation of the PR, as well as of every person subject to the Statutes, GRs
and Sport Rules, to be familiar with these provisions, and ignorance of them
does not exempt any person from liability.
19.11 In relation to points (ii) and (iii), the FEI highlighted that the PR duly signed the
FEI Sampling Form. The FEI Sampling Form expressly included the following
assertion: “I certify that I supervised the collection and sealing of the undermentioned
sample in accordance with the FEI Veterinary Regulations.” By signing this form, the
PR confirmed that the Sample Collection and sealing were properly conducted
in accordance with the applicable procedures. The FEI further noted that the PR
had the opportunity to record any alleged deviation from the Sampling
Procedure directly on the FEI Sampling Form. However, no such remark was ever
made. Consequently, the signed FEI Sampling Form and absence of any
recorded objection directly contradicted the PR’s allegation that the Sampling
Procedure was not properly conducted or supervised. In addition, the FEI further
confirmed with the Testing Veterinarian, Dr. Khaled AKL, that the name and
signature included in the FEI Sampling Form did correspond to the PR, and that
the PR was present during the complete Sampling Procedure.
20. The FEI also submitted that pursuant to Article 3.2.3 of the ECM Rules, “departures from
any provision of these Rules shall not invalidate analytical results or other evidence of an ECM
Rule violation; provided, however, that if the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support
Personnel and/or other Person establishes that a departure from a provision of these ECM
Rules could reasonably have caused the ECM Rule violation based on the Adverse Analytical
Finding or other ECM Rule violation, then the FEI shall have the burden to establish that such
departure did not cause the Adverse Analytical Finding or the factual basis for the ECM Rule
violation”.
6

21. In the present case, the FEI confirmed their opinion that the PR had failed to establish
the first requirement i.e., (a) the alleged procedural irregularities which subsequently
failed to establish the second requirement i.e., (b) that such alleged procedural
irregularities could reasonably have caused the ECM Rule violation in question.
Furthermore, the FEI noted that allegations require substantiating evidence. The FEI
noted that no evidence whatsoever has been submitted by the PR to demonstrate that
the alleged departures occurred and could have reasonably caused the Adverse
Analytical Finding.
22. Therefore, it was the FEI’s opinion that the burden of proof had not shifted to the FEI in
the sense of the above provision and that the Analytical Finding stands unopposed.
23. The FEI therefore considers that the source of the Adverse Analytical Finding has not
been established. As to Fault/Negligence for the Rule Violation, the starting point of any
evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following from Article 2.1.1 of the ECM Rules,
i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in
the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” It is also the
responsibility of the PR to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit all relevant
arguments regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any allegations
that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its presence.
24. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges brought forward by the
FEI. Consequently, it remained impossible, under the applicable rules, to evaluate the
PR’s degree of Fault or Negligence, if any. Consequently, the presumption of Fault as
stipulated in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules remains.
25. The FEI also stated that no elimination or reduction of the period of Ineligibility in this
case is possible and the applicable sanction for the current violation should be 6 (six)
months of Ineligibility in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules.
26. The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the PR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months on the PR, commencing from
the date of the Final Decision in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iii) disqualifying the result of the PR and Horse combination obtained in the Event,
and the consequent forfeiture of all medals, points, prize money, etc. won,
pursuant to Article 9 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iv) fining the PR in the amount of 3’500 CHF;
(v) ordering the PR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF that the FEI has incurred in
these proceedings.
V. Legal Analysis
7

A. Jurisdiction
27. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member
of the Saudi NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the PR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
28. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
29. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Sample taken
from the Horse at the Event. Triamcinolone Acetonide is a Controlled Medication
Substance and the presence of this substance in a horse’s system is prohibited under Article
2.1 of the ECM Rules.
30. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
PR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
31. The burden of proof then shifts to the PR. The standard of proof for the PR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the PR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) he bears No
(Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
8

32. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Triamcinolone Acetonide in the Horse’s
system, which constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI
satisfied its burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the
objective elements of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Elimination or Reduction of the Period of Ineligibility
33. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules. To benefit from
a reduction, the PR must establish, as a threshold requirement, how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system.3
34. Other than blanket denials, the PR did not submit any evidence establishing how the
Prohibited Substance entered into the Horse’s system. Therefore, the Tribunal finds that
the PR did not discharge his burden of proving how the Prohibited Substance entered
into the Horse’s system. The Tribunal therefore considers that the source of the Adverse
Analytical Finding has not been established.
35. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR following from Article
2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e., his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication
Substance is present in the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary
Form.” It is the responsibility of the PR to rebut the presumption of Fault and to submit
all relevant arguments regarding the source of the Prohibited Substance, as well as any
allegations that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence in relation to its
presence. In the present case, the PR has failed to respond to the charges brought
forward by the FEI. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the PR is not entitled to any
reduction of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of
the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
3 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
9

36. As the threshold criteria of source has not been proven, the Tribunal finds that the
applicable period of Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules,
which shall commence on the date of notification of this decision.
37. Pursuant to Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules, the results of the PR and the Horse
combination obtained in the entire Event are automatically disqualified, including
forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes.
38. The Tribunal also finds that given the PR’s apparent overall inexperience and lack of
experience with the process, that no purpose is served in imposing a large fine or legal
costs in this case. The Tribunal imposes a fine of CHF 2’000 on the PR and each party
will bear its own legal costs. If the PR’s stated financial circumstances are valid, the
Tribunal urges the FEI to work with the PR to develop a plan for payment of the fine.
VI. Terms of the Decision
39. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr ALQAHTANI violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Mr ALQAHTANI is suspended for a period of six (6) months. The period of the
Ineligibility will be effective from the date of notification of this decision.
c) Mr ALQAHTANI’s results at the Event with the Horse are disqualified, including the
forfeiture of any prize money, medals and ranking points.
d) Mr ALQAHTANI is ordered to pay a fine of two thousand Swiss Francs (CHF 2000).
e) Each party will bear its own legal costs.
40. Mr ALQAHTANI, the Saudi NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
41. Mr ALQAHTANI may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any capacity in a
Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any National
Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is authorized or
organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any capacity in
Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level event
organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
10

42. If Mr ALQAHTANI violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph during the
period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified and a new
period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will be added
to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions may be
imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
43. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
44. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
Ms Diane Pitts, Sole Panel Member

6. The FEI and the PR are together referred to as the Parties.
IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

and anxiety, at an estimated concentration of 3.5 ng/mL. O-desmethylvenlafaxine is a
metabolite of Venlafaxine. Venlafaxine is classified as a Banned Substance under the EADRs.
8. By Notification Letter dated 23 June 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the PR of
a potential violation of Article 2.1 of the EADRs (Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its
Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) based on the findings of O-desmethylvenlafaxine in
the sample. The PR was also notified in said letter that he was provisionally suspended under

• Shortly after notification of the AAF, on 27 June 2025, the PR contacted the Manager

until the PR was able to arrange for samples from Stall #28 to be collected for

• Several wipe samples were collected from Stall #28 on 6 August 2025. One of those

• Thus, the Horse’s stall at the Event was contaminated with Venlafaxine;
• The PR, along with other witnesses present, submitted that the stalls at the Event

DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
16 February 2026
In the matter of
Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh (APR; Ref. C25-0038)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT44 HURRICANE KAZAN)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Mr Brian Ward (CAN)

Prohibited Substance(s): Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh
committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled Medication
Rules – The Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s
Sample. The FEI notified Mr Singh of the alleged charge in his capacity as the Additional
Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh (FEI ID 10063972), was the registered trainer (the Additional
Person Responsible or the APR) of the horse Hurricane Kazan (FEI ID 108LI88, the Horse),
which competed in the CH-M-YH-E 120 8 YO – Jullianges, France held on 1 and 2 August
2025 (the Event).
5. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood and urine samples were collected from the Horse on 1 August 2025. The Horse’s
urine sample returned a positive finding for Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate.
2

7. Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate is a corticosteroid used in the treatment of severe allergic
reactions, endocrine and skin disorders. It is the hemisuccinate salt form of
Hydrocortisone and is thus of similar chemical structure and biological effect. It is
classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the 2025 FEI Equine Prohibited
Substances List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 4 September 2025, the FEI informed the APR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of
the ECM Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. Despite a reminder sent by the FEI to the APR via the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI)
and the Bahrain Royal Equestrian Federation (BEF), he did not submit a position nor did
he request the analysis of the B Sample. The B Sample was in any case requested by the
PR and the Owner of the Horse.
10. On 14 October 2025, the FEI informed the PR and the Owner of the Horse that the
analysis of the B Sample confirmed the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate.
11. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the FEI’s
Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
12. On 19 December 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel to
decide this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of
the Hearing Panel by 8 January 2025. In addition, the APR was invited to respond to the
FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence by
26 January 2026. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request
a hearing by 28 January 2026, at the latest.
13. The BEF confirmed to the Tribunal that the APR was provided a copy of the Notification
Letter and no response was received from the APR.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the APR
14. The APR elected to not submit any position.
1 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the FEI’s written submission.
3

B. Submissions by the FEI:
15. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
15.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample. As a strict
liability offence, it is not necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use
be demonstrated in order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
15.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies
the requirements of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
15.3 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that an Additional Person Responsible with
no previous ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is
subject to a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless he can rebut the
presumption of Fault on a balance of probability.
15.4 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the APR must establish
to the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the
Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate entered the Horse’s system. The APR must also
demonstrate one of the following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Banned Substance. If proven,
the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article 10.5 of
the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
15.5 The FEI submitted that since the APR failed to reply to the charges, he did not
establish how the Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate entered the Horse’s body, and it
is therefore not possible to evaluate his level of Fault or Negligence, if any, pursuant
to the applicable rules. As a consequence, the presumption of Fault as stipulated
in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall stand.
4

15.6 The FEI also stated that no elimination or reduction of the period of Ineligibility in
this case is possible and the applicable sanction for the current violation should be
6 (six) months of Ineligibility in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules
15.7 The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the APR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months on the APR, commencing from
the date of the Final Decision pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iii) fining the APR in the amount of 3’500 CHF (three thousand five hundred);
(iv) ordering the APR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF (two thousand) that the FEI
has incurred in these proceedings.
V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
16. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The APR is a member
of the EFI and the BEF, which are both members of the FEI; therefore, the APR is bound
by the ECM Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
17. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
18. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the Sample
taken from the Horse at the Event. Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate is a Controlled
Medication Substance and the presence of this substance in a horse’s system is prohibited
at all times under Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
5

19. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
APR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
20. The burden of proof then shifts to the APR. The standard of proof for the APR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the APR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and (ii) he bears No (Significant)
Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
ii. Anti-Doping Rule Violation
21. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the
Horse’s system, which constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore,
the FEI satisfied its burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the
objective elements of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Elimination or Reduction of the Period of Ineligibility
22. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules. To benefit from
a reduction, the APR must establish as a threshold requirement how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
23. The APR chose not to participate in the proceedings. Therefore, the Tribunal finds that
the APR did not discharge his burden of proving how the Prohibited Substance entered
the Horse’s system.
24. Where this first hurdle has not been met (i.e., establishing the source of the Prohibited
Substance), the Tribunal cannot continue with the second step and evaluate the APR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the APR is not
2 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
6

entitled to any reduction of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles
10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
25. As the threshold of source has not been proven, the Tribunal finds that the applicable
period of Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which
shall commence on the date of this decision.
26. The Tribunal also deems that the APR shall pay a fine of CHF 3,500 and pay CHF 2’000 to
the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
VI. Terms of the Decision
27. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is suspended for a period of six (6) months. The period
of the Ineligibility will be effective from the date of this decision.
c) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is ordered to pay a fine of three thousand five hundred
Swiss Francs (CHF 3,500).
d) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is ordered to pay two thousand Swiss francs (2’000 CHF)
to the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
28. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh, the Equestrian Federation of India, the Bahrain Royal
Equestrian Federation and the FEI will be notified this Decision. The Bahrain Royal
Equestrian Federation is requested to immediately transmit and notify the Decision to
Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh.
29. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any
capacity in a Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any
National Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is
authorized or organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any
capacity in Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level
event organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
7

30. If Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph
during the period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified
and a new period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will
be added to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions
may be imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
31. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
32. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
________________________________________
Mr Brian Ward, Sole Panel Member

title: FINAL DECISION C25-0026 SCHOONBROODT-DE AZEVEDO (2025 CM04 GRANIT DE LA MURE)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
18 March 2026
In the matter of
Ms Celine Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo (PR; Ref. C25-0026)
(FEI Case number: 2025/CM04 GRANIT DE LA MURE)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Diane Pitts (USA)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0026 [FEI 2025/ CM04 GRANIT DE LA MURE]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Celine SCHOONBROODT- DE AZEVEDO/10000938/ BEL
Horse/ID/NF: GRANIT DE LA MURE/107LT05/FRA
Event/Date/ID: CSI4* - Montefalco (ITA), 30.04-04.05.2025, 2025_CI_0945_S_S_03Date of
sample collection: 03.05.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Dexamethasone
Bar Code No.: 1555249

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Céline Schoonbroodt-De
Azevedo committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled
Medication Rules – The Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites
or Markers in a Horse’s Sample. The FEI notified Ms Schoonbroodt-De Azevedo of the
alleged charge in her capacity as the Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Céline SCHOONBROODT-DE AZEVEDO (FEI ID 0000938) is a Belgian Jumping Rider (the
Person Responsible or the PR), who competed with the horse Granit de la Mure (the
Horse), in the CSI4* Montefalco (ITA), held between 30 April and 4 May 2025 (the Event).
5. The FEI (together with the PR, the Parties), is the sole IOC-recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 3 May 2025. The Horse’s sample
returned a positive finding for Dexamethasone in its blood.
2

7. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and autoimmune
conditions. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI Equine
Prohibited Substances List.
8. The estimated concentration of Dexamethasone in the sample was estimated by the
Laboratory from the available data to be above the high positive control at 10 ng/mL. This
estimate was derived from a comparison of peak responses against the spiked positive
controls that were analysed alongside the sample.
9. The positive finding of Dexamethasone in the Horse’s Sample gives rise to a Controlled
Medication Rule Violation under the FEI ECM Rules (as no valid Veterinary Form was
submitted for the respective Prohibited Substance).
III. Procedural background
10. On 26 May 2025, the FEI informed the PR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM
Rules (the Notification Letter).
11. In the Notification Letter, the PR was informed that she had the right to request the
Horse's B Sample to be analysed, which she did, on 2 June 2025.
12. On 26 June 2025, the FEI informed the PR that the B Sample Analysis confirmed the
presence of the Prohibited Substance Dexamethasone in the Sample.
13. Following the Notification Letter, there were several exchanges between the FEI and the
PR’s lawyer in this matter, which ended in the PR choosing to have her case decided by
the FEI Tribunal.
14. Therefore, on 2 September 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the
FEI’s Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
15. On 9 September 2025, the PR asked the FEI Tribunal to indicate when the PR’s
argumentation for the hearing panel was expected. Furthermore, the PR requested,
pursuant to Article 20 of the IRs, that a hearing in this matter be conducted entirely in
French. Finally, the PR asked the composition of the hearing panel, in order to ensure
that there was no conflict with the FEI.
16. On 12 September 2025, the FEI Tribunal Chair acknowledged receipt of the Parties’
correspondences of 2 and 9 September 2025, respectively. In view of the PR’s request
for the hearing to be conducted in French, the FEI Tribunal Chair asked the FEI to submit
their position in this respect.
3

17. On 15 September 2025, the FEI informed the FEI Tribunal Chair that they did not agree
for the proceedings to be conducted in French. The FEI noted that all of the
communications in this case have been conducted so far solely in English (including the
PR submissions to the FEI and the PR’s witness testimonies), the FEI Response and the
accompanying Exhibits were filed in English and most importantly the Independent
Expert consulted by the FEI is an English speaker, provided his Expert Opinion in English
and relies on the study also published in English.
18. The PR submitted an additional position spontaneously, on 18 September 2025, insisting
on the proceedings to be conducted in French. The FEI Statutes stipulate that there are
two official languages, French and English, and hence the PR, who is French-speaking,
should have a right to have the proceedings held in French.
19. On 19 September 2025, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties that the proceedings
would be conducted in English, since the IRs provide that French can only apply if both
parties agree to it, which the FEI did not. The Tribunal Chair further informed the Parties
that he appointed a one-person Hearing Panel (“Panel”) to decide this case. The Parties
were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Panel by 22 September
2025. In addition, the PR was invited to respond to the FEI’s allegations by submitting a
statement of defence and any supporting evidence by 9 October 2025. Furthermore, the
Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request a hearing by 13 October
2025, at the latest.
20. On 19 September 2025, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Panel.
21. On 23 September 2025, the PR confirmed having no objection to the constitution of the
Panel, and requested an oral hearing, provided that no agreement were to be reached
by the parties until then.
22. On 9 October 2025, the PR filled her response to the FEI’s allegations and case file.
23. On 16 October 2025, the Tribunal asked the parties to clarify whether they requested a
hearing on the matter, since the PR, in her position, requested a hearing if the FEI did not
accept her proposal to limit her disqualification to three months. On the same day, the FEI
confirmed that they were seeking the sanctions to be imposed on the PR in accordance
with the FEI Response submitted on 2 September 2025.
24. On 20 October 2025, the PR confirmed her request for a hearing to take place, via
videoconference. The PR further requested for Dr Susanna Mazza to be heard as a
4

witness, objected to Dr Paine to be heard as he is not a direct witness to the facts, and
reserved her right to hear her employee, Mr Welson Pereira Da Silva. The PR also
regretted that the FEI refused to accept the 3-months reduction which the PR had agreed
to, provided the starting date was postponed. As a matter of fact, the PR, via her Counsel,
had informed the FEI that they agreed to the automatic 3-months reduction of the Period
of Ineligibility, provided that the Ineligibility would take effect only as of October 2025.
The FEI refused, stating that for the agreement to be accepted, the Period of Ineligibility
had to start immediately, i.e. as of August 2025. The PR considers the FEI’s position to be
unreasonable.
25. On 21 October 2025, the Panel acknowledged receipt of the Parties’ correspondences
and confirmed that a hearing would be held by videoconference. The Sole Panel Member
reminded the Parties that the hearing will be conducted in English, pursuant to Art. 20.2
of the IRs, and that any Party wishing to make submissions, or to rely on evidence, other
than English, must provide an independent interpreter at their own costs. While
reminding the Parties also about the rules governing the presence of witnesses at the
hearing, the Sole Panel Member asked the Parties to indicate who would be attending
the hearing, which witnesses they intended to rely upon, and for which witnesses or
parties an interpreter would be required. The Sole Panel Member also asked the Parties
to provide the name and credentials of the interpreter who would be officiating.
26. On 27 October 2025, the FEI informed the Tribunal that they would be represented at
the hearing by Ms Katarzyna Jozwik, FEI Legal Counsel; Ms Ana Kricej, FEI Senior Legal
Counsel and Ms Belen Flores Trelis, FEI Junior Legal Counsel. The FEI also requested the
testimony of Prof. Stuart Paine, expert in pharmacometrics at the School of Veterinary
Medicine and Science, University of Nottingham, Leicestershire (UK). Finally, the FEI
confirmed that no interpretation would be required for the hearing on their side.
27. On 27 October 2025, the PR’s Counsel informed the Tribunal that the PR would be
present at the hearing and he would assist her. The PR further requested for three
witnesses to be heard, i.e. Dr Susanna Mazza, Mr Welson Pereira Da Silva and Dr
Charlotte Seiffert from Equicare Group. Except for Mr Pereira Da Silva, all attendees
speak English. For Mr Pereira Da Silva, the PR indicated that they would manage to find a
translator from Portuguese to English.
28. After a few administrative exchanges among the Parties and the FEI Tribunal Clerk, the
agreed date for the hearing was fixed for the 11 December 2025.
29. On 11 November 2025, the Sole Panel Member confirmed said date, and mentioned to
the Parties the names of the witnesses who will be heard, in accordance with the Parties’
requests. The PR was further granted a deadline of 25 November 2025 to provide the
5

Tribunal with the name and credentials of the Portuguese – English interpreter. Finally,
the Sole Panel Member proposed a hearing schedule for the hearing.
30. On 14 November 2025, the PR’s Counsel indicated that she will not pay for an official
translator, and would find someone Brazilian, probably from her stable, to do the
translation or would do it herself, because finding an official interpreter would be too
costly. The PR reiterated her objection for the proceedings to be conducted in English,
since the FEI Statutes stipulate that the two official languages are English and French. The
choice of English as the language of the proceedings is therefore an obstacle to the PR’s
ability to defend her rights. Finally, the PR asked from where the Sole Panel Member
would attend the hearing, requesting confirmation that she would not be present at the
FEI premises.
31. The FEI agreed on 18 November 2025 that the translator in this case does not need to
be a professional translator, provided the person is independent and has sufficient
knowledge of both languages. The FEI was opposed, however, to the PR, her Counsel, or
any person related to her, serving as interpreter.
32. On 20 November 2025, the Tribunal Clerk acknowledged receipt of the Parties’ respective
correspondences, and informed the PR that the Sole Panel Member will indeed be
connected remotely from the US, and will not be at the FEI’s premises.
33. The hearing took place as scheduled on 11 December 2025.
34. On 6 January 2026, the Sole Panel Member requested additional positions from the
Parties, enclosing an article of the British Horse Racing Authority (BHA), which is an
acknowledged source in the FEI List of Detection Times. The Parties were asked to
comment on the detection times mentioned in said article, as they relate to
dexamethasone.
35. On 16, respectively 17 January 2026, the FEI and the PR submitted their additional
position as requested by the Sole Panel Member.
36. On 22 January 2026, the Sole Panel Member acknowledged receipt of the Parties’
submissions and informed them that a decision on the matter would be notified in due
course.
37. On 12 February 2026, the PR asked for an update on the matter.
38. On 13 February 2026, the Sole Panel Member issued the operative part of the decision.
6

IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the PR
39. On 9 October 2025, the PR submitted her position to the Tribunal, which can be
summarised as follows:
39.1 After having received the Notification Letter, the PR requested for the B-Sample
analysis.
39.2 After having received the results of the B-Sample analysis – which confirmed the
A-Sample analysis – the PR sent her position to the FEI, which requested
additional information on 21 July 2025. The PR submitted her additional position
to the FEI on 11 August 2025.
39.3 The PR is a Jumping Rider from Belgium, ranked 153rd in the World. She has
participated in 2809 international jumping competitions since 1 January 2010.
39.4 The PR has no prior ECM Rule Violation for purposes of Article 10.9 of the ECM
Rules.
39.5 The Horse arrived at the Event’s venue before the PR, on 28 April 2025, but was
accompanied by the groom, Mr Pereira Da Silva (the Groom). Indeed, the PR had
to fly urgently to Brazil on 23 April 2025 for personal reasons.
39.6 When the PR arrived at the Event’s venue, on 29 April 2025, the Groom did not
inform her of anything concerning treatment of her horses.
39.7 After receipt of the positive findings, the PR investigated to understand what had
happened. The Groom confessed to the PR, in the end of June 2025, that he had
called a veterinarian, Dr Susanna Mazza, on 28 April 2025 as the Horse was
having an allergic reaction.
39.8 Dr Mazza confirmed that she had examined the Horse and, due to the symptoms
he was showing, injected him with 15 ml of Dexadreson, and performed fluid
therapy (5L). At the hearing, where she appeared as a witness, she further

V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
41. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member
of the Belgian NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the PR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
42. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
43. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the A Sample and the B Sample reflect that the analytical tests
were performed in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal
is further satisfied that the test results evidence the presence of Dexamethasone in the
Sample taken from the Horse at the Event. Dexamethasone is a Controlled Medication
Substance and the presence of this substance in a horse’s system is prohibited under Article
2.1 of the ECM Rules.
16

44. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Panel notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the PR
committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to prove
intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
45. The burden of proof then shifts to the PR. The standard of proof for the PR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the PR
to avoid or reduce a six (6) month sanction, she must establish, on a balance of
probability: (i) how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) she
bears No (Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM
Rules.
ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
46. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Dexamethasone in the Horse’s system,
which constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI satisfied
its burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the objective
elements of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Length of the Period of Ineligibility and evaluation of Fault
47. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules, or to an increase
of the Period of Ineligibility in cases of Aggravating Circumstances pursuant to Article 10.4
of the ECM Rules. To benefit from a reduction, the PR must establish as a threshold
requirement how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
48. In the present case, it was the PR’s explanation that the Prohibited Substance found in
the Horse’s system came from an injection performed by a veterinarian on-site, Dr
Susanna Mazza, on 28 April 2025. The injection happened before the PR arrived at the
Event, without her knowing about it, and the quantity injected was 15 ml of Dexadreson,
in addition to fluid therapy.

49. The FEI contested this explanation, considering that it was not plausible. The FEI based
their reasoning on Dr Suart Paine’s Expert Opinion, which explained, scientifically, that
the PR’s account of events was not possible, in view of the amount of dexamethasone
which remained in the Horse’s system at the time of the blood test. As a matter of fact,
Dr Paine explained that 15 ml injection of Dexadreson is equivalent to 30 milligram dose
of Dexamethasone. In the present case, the concentration in the Horse’s blood was of
10 ng/ml, which is a very high concentration, which would be expected 4-6 hours after a
30-milligram administration by injection. Not, as the PR alleges, 5 days after said injection.
50. The above is further evidenced by the Figure 2a submitted by the FEI, resulting from the
scientific literature, i.e. Soma, Uboh, Liu, Li, Robinson, Boston & Colahan:
Pharmacokinetics of dexamethasone following intra-articular, intravenous, intramuscular,
and oral administration in horses and its effects on endogenous hydrocortisone; Journal of
Veterinary Pharmacology and Therapeutics 36, 181-191. On said figure, which is part of
the file, one can see that the plasma concentration, in ng/ml, declines quickly below the
10 ng/ml, after 4-6 hours, to be almost nil after 48 hours, i.e. 2 days. The Panel
acknowledges that different horses metabolise substances at different rates and that
detection times and levels have been acknowledged to vary in horses. However, in the
present case, in the Panel’s view, the PR’s allegation that this concentration of 10 ng/ml
would still be present 5 days after the injection performed by the veterinarian, is not
plausible, in the balance of probabilities.
Furthermore, the Panel weighed the witnesses’ credibility in reaching this conclusion. In
particular, the Panel noted that the version of the events from various witnesses differed.
For instance, Dr Mazza clearly indicated that she had told the Groom “no competition”,
to which he himself answered “no competition”. This might be plausible, because even
though the Groom alleged not to speak English, the Portuguese equivalent of “no
competição”, is very similar to the English word “no competition”. But the Groom denied
having heard, or pronounced, those words. Similarly, while the PR indicated having only
heard about this story upon receipt of the Notification Letter from the FEI on 29 May
2025, Dr Seiffert originally testified that the PR had actually called her, in the week or so
after the Event which ended on 4 May 2025, to explain that there had been an issue
with this Horse, while still being in Italy.
51. The Sole Panel Member wishes to emphasise that she did not find the PR not credible,
or untruthful, but the abovementioned discrepancies from the PR’s own witnesses added
to the doubts, which could not be overturned in the Panel’s mind. The main issue in the
present case is that scientific explanations do not support the PR’s account of events.
And consequently, the Sole Panel Member cannot be comfortably satisfied that the PR
proved how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s body.
18

52. Where this first hurdle has not been met (i.e., establishing the source of the Prohibited
Substance), the Tribunal cannot continue with the second step and evaluate the PR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence.
53. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the PR, i.e., her personal duty
to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in the Horse’s body during
an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” It is also the responsibility of the PR to rebut the
presumption of Fault and to submit all relevant arguments regarding the source of the
Prohibited Substance, as well as any allegations that he or she bears No (Significant) Fault
or Negligence in relation to its presence. In the present case, the PR has failed to prove, to
the comfortable satisfaction of the Panel, how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s
system. Consequently, it remains impossible, under the applicable rules, to evaluate the PR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence, if any. Consequently, the presumption of Fault as stipulated
in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall stand, and the PR is not entitled to any reduction
of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM
Rules.
54. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the PR is not entitled to any reduction of the
otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
55. In view of the above considerations, the Tribunal finds that the applicable period of
Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which shall
commence on the date of notification of this decision.
56. Pursuant to Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules, the results of the PR and the Horse
combination obtained in the entire Event are automatically disqualified, including
forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes.
57. However, the Sole Panel Member will not impose any fine or costs on the PR. Indeed,
while, on the balance of probabilities, the Panel was not sufficiently satisfied that the PR
proved how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system, this results from a
lack of consistency in view of the scientific literature and detection and withdrawal times.
However, the Panel was not insensitive to the PR’s argument that she was not aware that
Dexamethasone had been administered to her Horse when she arrived at the Event. It
remains unclear whether, perhaps, it was a much larger amount which was administered
to the Horse on 28 April 2025, or if it was administered at a later date than the one alleged
by the PR. In any event, the Sole Panel Member is therefore of the view that fairness
19

dictates, pursuant to the FEI Guidelines on Fines and contributions towards legal costs,
that no fine and no proceedings costs be levied in the present matter.
58. However, the above does not apply to the costs related to the B Sample analysis, which
will have to be borne by the PR, as it is standard for every time that the B Sample analysis
is requested by a PR.
59. Therefore, each party will bear their own procedural and legal costs, and no fine is
imposed on the PR. The PR will only bear the costs of the B-Sample analysis, which
amount to CHF 1’000.-.
VI. Terms of the Decision
60. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Ms Celine Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Ms Celine Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo is suspended for a period of six (6)
months. The period of the Ineligibility will be effective from the date of
notification of this decision.
c) The results of the PR and Horse combination at the Event are disqualified, and
the medals, points, prize money, etc. won at the Event are forfeited, pursuant
to Article 9 and 10.1.2 of the ECM Rules.
d) No fine is imposed on Ms Celine Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo.
e) Each Party will bear its own legal costs.
f) Ms Celine Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo is ordered to pay one thousand Swiss
francs (1’000 CHF) to the FEI as costs of the B Sample analysis.
61. Ms Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo, the Belgian NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
62. Ms Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in
any capacity in a Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any
National Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is
authorized or organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any
capacity in Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level
event organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
20

63. If Ms Schoonbroodt-de Azevedo violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph
during the period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified
and a new period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will
be added to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions
may be imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
64. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
65. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
