title: Final Decision Settlement Agreement C26-0002 2025 BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS (MANDILLE)
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY THE FEI TRIBUNAL
11 February 2026
In the matter of
FÉDÉRATION EQUESTRE INTERNATIONALE (the “FEI”)
vs.
Ms Astrid MANDILLE – Person Responsible (the “PR”)
together the “Parties”
(Reference No. FEI Tribunal: C26-0002 MANDILLE)
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Ms Harveen Thauli (CAN), Sole Panel Member
FEI Case number: 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS
Horse/Passport: GABOR DE FLORYS/109FJ44/FRA
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Astrid MANDILLE/10349599/FRA
Event/Date: Pony Measuring Session, Ludon-Médoc, France
Date of sample collection: 28.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Bromazepam
Bar Code No.: 1608996
1

All the words used in this Final Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the FEI General Regulations
(the “GRs”) and Statutes, the FEI Veterinary Regulations (the “VRs”), the 2025 Equine
Prohibited Substance List (the “FEI Prohibited List”), and the Equine Anti-Doping and
Controlled Medication Regulations (the “EADCMRs”). The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the
“EAD Rules”) and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the “ECM Rules”) are set out in
the EADCMRs.
I. Introduction
1. This Final Decision pertains to the FEI case, 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS. In this
matter, the FEI notified the PR that a violation of Article 2.1 (The Presence of a Banned
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the
Use of a Banned Substance and/or Banned Method) of the EAD Rules had occurred
based on the positive finding of Bromazepam in the Sample of the horse, Gabor de
Florys (the “Horse”), which was collected when the Horse was presented for Pony
Measurement in Ludon-Médoc (France) on 28 April 2025 (the “Event”).
2. The FEI and the PR agreed to a Settlement Agreement on 26 January 2026 (the
“Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement together with the attached
Exhibits are hereby incorporated by reference in this Final Decision.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions
3. The following regulations are applicable to the present case:
Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
General Regulations, 24thedition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2025.
(the “GRs”).
Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (the “IRs”).
FEI Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations, 4th edition, effective
1 January 2025 (the “EADCMRs”). As only the EAD Rules apply in the present case,
reference will be made hereinafter only to this second chapter of the EADCMRs.
FEI Veterinary Regulations, 15th edition 2023, effective 1 January 2025 (the “VRs”).
2

III. Factual background and initial proceedings
4. Ms Astrid MANDILLE (FEI ID 10349599) is the Horse’s owner, and the PR in
accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs.
5. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-
Driving, Endurance and Vaulting.
6. The PR is a member of the French Equestrian Federation (the “FRA-NF”), the latter
being a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EAD Rules.
7. The Horse was tested during the Event and returned a positive finding of
Bromazepam, which is an anxiolytic used in the treatment of anxiety and insomnia.
Bromazepam is classified as a Banned Substance, prohibited at all times, under the
FEI Prohibited List.
8. Therefore, the positive findings of Bromazepam in the Sample gave rise to a
violation of the EAD Rules (the “EAD Rule Violation”).
9. The FEI informed the PR of the EAD Rule Violation in a notification letter dated 2 June
2025 (the “Notification Letter”). In accordance with Article 7.4.1. of the EAD Rules,
the FEI provisionally suspended the PR as at the date of the Notification Letter (the
“Provisional Suspension”).
10. The PR had the right to request an analysis of the B Sample. The PR did not request
its analysis; therefore, she irrevocably waived this right.
11. In the Notification Letter, the FEI further informed the PR of her right to provide an
explanation within 20 days from the date of the Notification Letter.
12. The PR provided statements to the FEI where she explained how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system. The Horse, owned by the PR since 2022, is
a pony stallion. The Horse is reluctant to compete and stops at the entrance of the
arena, rearing up (a behaviour the Horse had already displayed before the PR
purchased him). After the purchase, the Horse spent two years in the pasture
without any work. The PR hoped that, after this period of rest, he would be willing
to resume competing over small 90 cm obstacles, but this has not been the case. In
February 2025, the PR signed an agreement with a third party, whereby the Horse
would be loaned to said third party, free of charge, for the purpose of breeding
(inseminating) a mare. Under this agreement, the Horse was moved to a Chateau,
where he lived in the same paddock as the mare. The PR decided to bring the Horse
3

to the Pony Measuring Session because it was held very close to the Chateau, and
she believed that having an official measurement certificate would be useful for the
potential approval of the Horse as a breeding stallion. Following receipt of the
Notification Letter, the PR inquired with the mare’s owner about the source of the
Prohibited Substance. The owner explained that the mare is a pony suffering from
behavioural disorders and that he had administered Regumate (Altrenogest) and
Lexomil (Bromazepam) to her. The mare was under treatment when the Horse was
at the Chateau. The PR submitted a veterinary prescription document issued on 7
January 2025 certifying that the mare was diagnosed with hormone-dependent
behavioural disorders. The prescription includes the oral administration of
Regumate (1 dose per 400 kg, once per day for six months), as well as Lexomil 6 mg
(4 tablets per day for a period of 6 to 8 months). The two ponies lived together in
the same paddock and were fed with grain and hay. There was no system in place
to check or control the feed. The PR submitted that the gardener may have
accidentally switched the feed buckets, resulting in the Horse unintentionally
ingesting the Prohibited Substance.
13. After reviewing the PR’s submissions and evidence, the FEI was satisfied that the PR
had established, on a balance of probabilities, that the source of the Prohibited
Substances was Regumate and Lexomil, which had been administered to the mare
at the Chateau where the Horse was staying. Lexomil contains Bromazepam, which
is the Prohibited Substance at issue in this matter. Therefore, the FEI considered
that the PR had established how the Prohibited Substances entered the Horse’s
body.
14. Furthermore, the FEI was satisfied that the PR had established, pursuant to Article
10.6 of the EAD Rules, that she bore “No Significant Fault or Negligence” for the EAD
Rule Violation1.
15. On 26 January 2026, the FEI notified the Tribunal that it had reached a settlement
of the dispute with the PR, which included the reduction of the period of Ineligibility
to be imposed on the PR.
16. On 2 February 2026, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a one-
person hearing panel (the “Hearing Panel”) to adjudicate and approve this case. The
Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the Hearing
Panel by 5 February 2026.
17. On 3 February 2026, the FEI confirmed having no objection to the constitution of
1 Paragraphs 2.4 to 2.16 of the Settlement Agreement dated 21 January 2026 between the FEI and the PR together with the
Exhibits referenced therein evaluate the PR’s level of Fault and Negligence for the EAD Rule Violation.
4

the Hearing Panel.
18. The PR did not submit any objection to the constitution of the Hearing Panel.
IV. Accepted Terms
19. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EAD
Rules and is subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
20. The PR explicitly admitted the EAD Rule Violation and accepted the following terms
(the “Accepted Terms”) in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EAD Rules:
a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 of the EAD Rules (The presence of a
Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s Sample).
b) The PR established on a balance of probabilities how Bromazepam entered
the Horse’s system.
c) The PR bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for the EAD Rule Violation,
in accordance with article 10.6 of the EAD Rules.
d) The applicable period of Ineligibility is eighteen (18) months, in accordance
with article 10.6.2 of the EAD Rules, commencing as at the date of this Final
Decision (the Provisional Suspension already served will be credited against
the imposed period of Ineligibility).
e) The FEI Lifetime Measuring Certificate received at the Event is invalidated.
f) The PR will pay a fine of 500 CHF.
g) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with
these proceedings.
h) No other Sanctions will apply in this case.
i) The EAD Rule Violation is considered a prior violation for the purpose of
Multiple Violations in accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EAD Rules.
V. Decision
21. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes,
Article 159 of the GRs, the EAD Rules, the VRs and Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a
member of the FRA-NF, which is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by
the EAD Rules.
22. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement
5

and the Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel takes note that the FEI has agreed that
the PR established, on a balance of probabilities, how Bromazepam entered the
Horse’s system.
23. The Hearing Panel further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on
the terms to conclude these proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the
EAD Rules, as detailed under Section IV of this Final Decision.
24. The Hearing Panel confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement
comply with the EAD Rules and finds no grounds to object to them.
25. In particular, the Hearing Panel notes that, in view of the Settlement Agreement
reached by the parties that the PR bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for the
EAD Rule Violation, the period of Ineligibility imposed on the PR is reduced to a
period of eighteen months, starting as at the date of the Provisional Suspension.
26. Therefore, and in accordance with the mutual consent of the Parties, the Hearing
Panel hereby directs the Parties to fully comply with all the terms of the Settlement
Agreement. Furthermore, this Final Decision concludes this case, C26-0002
MANDILLE, 2025/BS06 GABOR DE FLORYS.
27. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 13.3 of the EAD Rules,
this Final Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the Settlement
Agreement are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject matter
of these proceedings.
28. The Settlement Agreement and this Final Decision are not subject to appeal under
Article 12 of the EAD Rules.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
b. The Secretary General of the NF of the person sanctioned: Yes
c. Any other: No
FOR THE FEI TRIBUNAL
_______________________________________________
Ms Harveen Thauli, One-Member Panel

title: FINAL DECISION C25-0033 ALDUWAYHI (2025 FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
19 January 2026
In the matter of
Mr Nasser ALDHUWAYHI (APR; Ref. C25-0033)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Ms Yuri Yagi (JPN)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0033 [FEI 2025/ FT30 AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Saad ALQAHTANI/10262539/KSA
Horse/ID/NF: AZZAM ALSHAYTHAM/108CG12/KSA
Trainer/ID/NF: Nasser ALDHUWAYHI/10255516/KSA
Event/Date/ID: CEI1* 100 - Riyadh (KSA), 24-26.04, 2025_CI_0266_E_S_02
Date of sample collection: 26.04.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Flunixin
Bar Code No.: 1417795

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Nasser ALDHUWAYHI
committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled Medication
Rules – The Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers
in a Horse’s Sample. The FEI notified Mr ALDHUWAYHI of the alleged charge in his capacity
as the Additional Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Nasser ALDHUWAYHI (FEI ID 10255516) is a Saudi Trainer (the Additional Person
Responsible or the APR), who was the registered trainer of the horse Azzam Alshaytham
(the Horse), which competed, with its rider, Saad ALQAHTANI, in the CEI1* 100 – Riyadh
(KSA), held on 24-26 April 2025 (the Event).
5. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood samples were collected from the Horse on 26 April 2025. The Horse’s sample
returned a positive finding for Flunixin in its blood.
2

7. Flunixin is non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication used to relieve pain, inflammation
and control fever. It is classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI
Equine Prohibited Substances List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 30 June 2025, the FEI informed the APR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of the
ECM Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. The APR submitted his explanations by way of correspondences dated 9, 10 and 13 July
2025 to the FEI.
10. In accordance with Article 8.3.6 of the ECM Rules, if the Person Responsible and/or
member of the Support Personnel (where applicable) does not elect the Administrative
Procedure within the fixed time limit, the Administrative Sanctions shall be considered
declined and the case shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal for final Decision.
11. In the present case, the APR did not elect the Administrative Procedure within the fixed
time limit. Therefore, on 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case
file (the FEI’s Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
12. On 17 October 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel to decide
this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of the
Hearing Panel by 20 October 2025. In addition, the APR was invited to respond to the
FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence by 6
November 2025. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request
a hearing by 10 November 2025, at the latest.
13. On 17 October 2025, both Parties confirmed having no objection to the constitution of
the Panel.
14. The APR did not file a submission or request a hearing despite having been notified the
Tribunal’s letter via email directly to him and through the Saudi NF.
15. On 12 November 2025, the Sole Panel Member acknowledged receipt of the Parties’
respective correspondences. The Sole Panel Member, noted that the APR confirmed
having no objection to the constitution of the Panel, but later did not submit any position
within the prescribed deadline. Accordingly, for the sake of good order and considering
that the APR was not represented by Counsel, the Sole Panel Member decided to grant
3

an exceptional and ultimate deadline to the APR to submit his reply to the FEI’s Response,
by 17 November 2025.
16. Again, the APR did not submit any position. Therefore, on 2 December 2025, the Sole
Panel Member noted the absence of position, and informed the parties that a Final
Decision, based on the file in its possession, will be notified to the Parties in due course.
17. In response to the Sole Panel Member’s 2 December 2025 letter, the APR indicated that
he had already answered “more than once” to the email sent.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the APR
18. The APR elected to not submit any position in front of the Tribunal. His submissions in
front of the FEI can be summarised as follows:
18.1 On 9 July 2025, the APR submitted via e-mail that on 26 April 2025 following the
completion of the second loop, the Horse was administered Finadyne together
with half a litre of 50% glucose solution, saline, and Ringer’s solution allegedly as
an emergency measure due to its poor health condition caused by extreme heat.
According to the APR, thereafter, the Treating Veterinarian took over the
treatment and administered Dexamethasone and intravenous fluids.
18.2 Following question posed by the FEI, the APR admitted that he had personally
administered the substance, given the Horse’s health condition.
18.3 The APR justified the administration of the Prohibited Substance as a necessary
measure to safeguard the Horse’s life and welfare, after it collapsed due to
extreme heat (43°C) despite having passed the veterinary inspection. The APR
submitted that the treatment given to the Horse was a painkiller.
18.4 Despite the FEI’s response reminding that the presence of a Controlled
Medication Substance in a Horse’s sample without a valid Veterinary Form
constitutes a Controlled Medication Rule Violation, and further clarifying that
emergency treatments with Controlled Medication Substances are permitted
under the FEI Veterinary Regulations provided that they are administered by a
veterinarian and duly authorized through a retrospective Veterinary Form A
signed by the Veterinary Delegate/Veterinary Commission and the Ground Jury
1 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the Parties’ written submissions.
4

before the end of the Event, the APR neither provided further reply nor accepted
the Administrative Procedure.
B. Submissions by the FEI:
19. On 10 October 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
19.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample without a valid
Veterinary Form. The same article also provides that Support Personnel may be
regarded as “Additional Persons Responsible under this Article and Articles 2.2-2.5
ECM Rules where the circumstances so warrant”. As a strict liability offence, it is not
necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use be demonstrated in
order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
19.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Flunixin in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies the requirements of
Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
19.3 Article 118.3 of the GRs establishes that, “the Person Responsible shall be the
Athlete who rides […] the Horse during an Event […].” The PR is the Athlete who rode
the Horse at the Event.
19.4 The Preface to the EADCM Regulations specifies that 'in the discipline of
Endurance, the registered Trainer shall be considered as additional Person
Responsible and held additionally responsible for any violation(s) under Articles
2.1 of the EAD Rules and the ECM Rules.
19.5 This principle is further reflected in Article 118.3 of the FEI General Regulations
(the GRs), which establishes that “the Person Responsible shall be the Athlete who
rides, vaults or drives the Horse during an Event, but the Owner and other Support
Personnel including but not limited to grooms and veterinarians may be regarded as
additional Persons Responsible if they are present at the Event or have made a
relevant Decision about the Horse. In vaulting, the lunger shall be an additional
Person Responsible. In Endurance, the Trainer shall be the additional Person
Responsible.”
19.6 Accordingly, under the applicable rules, the Trainer in Endurance is expressly
designated as an Additional Person Responsible, alongside the Person
Responsible.
5

19.7 The FEI does not submit any request for the disqualification of the results
obtained by the PR and the Horse during the Event, since this was requested in
the procedure against the PR.
19.8 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that a Person Responsible with no previous
ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is subject to a
period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless he can rebut the presumption of Fault
on a balance of probability.
19.9 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the APR must establish
to the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the Flunixin
entered the Horse’s system. The APR must also demonstrate one of the following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Prohibited Substance. If
proven, the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article
10.5 of the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
19.10 The ECM Rules stipulate, and the jurisprudence of the FEI Tribunal and the CAS is
very clear: It is a strict threshold requirement of any plea of No (or No Significant)
Fault or Negligence that the APR proves how the Prohibited Substance entered
into the Horse's system. In this context, the APR must provide clear and convincing
evidence that prove how the Flunixin entered the Horse’s body.
19.11 In this regard, the APR has expressly admitted that he personally administered
Flunixin (Finadyne/Fenadine) to the Horse on 26 April 2025 following the
completion of the second loop. The FEI therefore considers that the source of the
Adverse Analytical Finding has been established by the APR.
19.12 The starting point of any evaluation of the Fault / Negligence for the Rule Violation
is the “personal duty” of the APR following from Article 2.1.1 of the ECM Rules, i.e.,
his personal duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in
the Horse’s body during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” The definition
of Fault is provided for in Appendix 1 of the EADCM Rules.
6

19.13 To verify the APR’s explanations, the FEI contacted the President of the Treating
Veterinary Commission (the PTVC) at the Event, and who treated the Horse as per
the Veterinary Form A. The PTVC confirmed that when he reached the Horse, it was
found collapsed and lying down. However, the PTVC also confirmed that he
reached the Horse within less than two minutes of being notified, as the clinic was
located only 100 metres from the stables of the holding area. In addition, the PTVC
confirmed that, upon his inquiry, the APR initially denied the administration of any
medication prior to his (i.e., PTVC’s) arrival and reported that the Horse had
suddenly collapsed. Subsequently, the APR informed the PTVC that a spectator had
administered an injection which he later identified to be Flunixin, although the APR
had not been initially aware of this.
19.14 The FEI submitted that the APR expressly admitted to the FEI that he personally
administered the substance to the Horse, which contradicts the information
initially provided to the PTVC.
19.15 The FEI emphasize that this case concerns (i) an in-competition administration of a
Prohibited Substance without a valid Veterinary Form A and (ii) an administration
by a non-authorised person, which to the best knowledge of the FEI is not a
licensed veterinarian and/or does not hold the necessary and formal qualification
to be able to correctly and safely administer medication by injection.
19.16 In relation to point (i), the gravity of an unauthorized in-competition administration
of a Controlled Medication is significantly higher compared to an out-of-
competition administration, where the Horse might not have completely
eliminated the substance by the time of the competition, and may therefore test
positive as a result of a miscalculation of the Detection and/or Withdrawal Times
by the administering person. FEI Events are fully supported to carry out
(emergency) treatments of horses by authorized and qualified veterinarians, if the
need arises.
19.17 In relation to point (ii), it is extremely reckless and dangerous for a person without
the necessary qualifications to be injecting a horse. If done incorrectly, the horse
can sustain serious consequences and may even lose its life.
19.18 The sole justification advanced by the APR for the in-competition administration of
Flunixin (Finadyne) was the alleged need to safeguard the Horse’s health following
its collapse due to extreme heat. However, the FEI Veterinary Regulations expressly
provide for such emergency situations to be addressed through treatment by
accredited veterinarians and the subsequent submission of a retrospective
Veterinary Form A duly authorised by the Veterinary Delegate/Veterinary
7

Commission and the Ground Jury. In the present case, the PTVC who treated the
Horse confirmed that the clinic was only 100 meters away from where the Horse
had collapsed, and that he attended to the Horse within two minutes of being
notified of its collapse. Therefore, in the FEI’s opinion there was no reason
whatsoever for the unauthorized administration by the APR and the FEI does not
acknowledge the APR’s justifications.
19.19 In light of the applicable rules, the explanations put forward by the APR do not
justify the reduction of degree of Fault. Accordingly, the FEI finds that neither the
circumstances invoked by the APR warrant any mitigation of the applicable
sanction, nor can they support a finding of No Fault or Negligence, or No Significant
Fault or Negligence under the EADCM Regulations. As a consequence, the
presumption of Fault as stipulated in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall stand.
19.20 Article 10.4 of the ECM Rules provides that a greater period of ineligibility than the
standard sanction may be imposed if the FEI establishes, in an individual case
involving an ECM Rule violation under article 2.1, that Aggravating Circumstances
are present. The period of ineligibility shall be increased by an additional period of
Ineligibility of up to six (6) months depending on the seriousness of the violation,
unless the PR/APR can establish that they did not knowingly commit the ECM Rule
Violation.
19.21 The FEI submitted that the APR failed to provide truthful information to the PTVC
at the time of the incident. Furthermore, the administration of a Controlled
Medication substance to a Horse by a person who is not authorized to do so
constitutes a grave violation, and does not only breaches the VRs, but also causes
a significant risk to the Horse’s health and welfare.
19.22 In light of the above circumstances, the FEI is of the opinion that there are
aggravating factors, which justify an increase of the period of ineligibility to seven
(7) months in accordance with Article 10.4 of the ECM Rules.
19.23 The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the APR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of seven (7) months on the APR, commencing
from the date of the Final Decision in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM
Rules;
(iii) fining the APR in the amount of 5’000 CHF;
(iv) ordering the APR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF that the FEI has incurred in
these proceedings.
8

V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
20. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The APR is a member
of the Saudi NF, which is a member of the FEI; therefore, the APR is bound by the ECM
Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
21. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
22. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Flunixin in the Sample taken from the Horse
at the Event. Flunixin is a Controlled Medication Substance and the presence of this
substance in a horse’s system is prohibited at all times under Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
23. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
APR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
24. The burden of proof then shifts to the APR. The standard of proof for the APR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the APR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and that (ii) he bears No
(Significant) Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.

ii. Controlled Medication Rule Violation
25. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Flunixin in the Horse’s system, which
constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore, the FEI satisfied its
burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the objective elements
of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Length of the Period of Ineligibility and evaluation of Fault
26. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules, or to an increase
of the Period of Ineligibility in cases of Aggravating Circumstances pursuant to Article 10.4
of the ECM Rules. To benefit from a reduction, the APR must establish as a threshold
requirement how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
27. In the present case, the APR admitted having administered himself the Prohibited
Substance to the Horse. The Sole Panel Member is therefore satisfied that the APR
established, on a balance of probabilities, how the Prohibited Substance entered the
Horse’s system, which is moreover not disputed by the FEI.
28. Where this first hurdle has been met (i.e., establishing the source of the Prohibited
Substance), the Tribunal must continue with the second step and evaluate the APR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence.
29. The starting point of any evaluation is the “personal duty” of the APR, i.e., his personal
duty to ensure that “no Controlled Medication Substance is present in the Horse’s body
during an Event without a valid Veterinary Form.” In this respect, it is necessary to look at
the definitions of Fault and Negligence, as defined in Appendix 1 of the EADCM
Regulations:
‘Fault. Fault is any breach of duty or any lack of care appropriate to a particular situation.
Factors to be taken into consideration in assessing an Person Responsible and/or member of
the Support Personnel’s and/or other Person’s degree of Fault include, for example, the Person
Responsible’s and/or member of the Support Personnel’s and/or other Person’s experience,
whether the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support Personnel and/or other Person

‘No Fault or Negligence. The Persons Responsible and/or members of the Support Personnel
and/or other Persons establishing that they did not know or suspect, and could not reasonably

Substance or they had Used on the Horse, a Banned or Controlled Medication Method or
otherwise violated an EAD or ECM Rule. Except in the case of a Minor, for any violation of Article
2.1, the Athlete must also establish how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system’.
‘No Significant Fault or Negligence. The Person Responsible and/or member of the Support
Personnel establishing that their fault or negligence, when viewed in the totality of the
circumstances and taking into account the criteria for No Fault or Negligence, was not
significant in relationship to the EADCM Regulation violation. Except in the case of a Minor, for
any violation of Article 2.1 of the EAD Rules and Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, the Person
Responsible must also establish how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system’.
30. In the present matter, the Sole Panel Member notes that, while the APR admitted, in front
of the FEI, having administered himself the Prohibited Substance, he had initially denied
the administration of any medication prior to the PTVC’s arrival, and subsequently alleged
that it was a spectator who had administered an injection.
31. In front of the FEI, the APR justified the administration of the Prohibited Substance with
the need to safeguard the Horse’s health and safety following its collapse due to extreme
heat. However, as the PTVC indicated to the FEI, the clinic was only 100 meters away from
where the Horse had collapsed, and the PTVC arrived in less than two minutes after
having been called. Therefore, the Sole Panel Member agrees with the FEI that there was
no reason whatsoever for the unauthorized administration of the Prohibited Substance
by the APR.

32. Not only was it not justified, but what is more concerning is the fact that the APR
administered a Prohibited Substance to his Horse, as a non-authorized person, while –
to the best of the FEI’s knowledge, which has not been rebutted by the APR – the APR is
not a licensed veterinarian and/or does not hold the necessary and formal qualifications
to be able to correctly and safely administer medication by injection.
33. The Sole Panel Member further agrees with the FEI that the gravity of an unauthorized
in-competition administration is higher than an out-of-competition administration, where
the Horse might not have completely eliminated the substance by the time of the
competition, and may therefore test positive as a result, for instance, of a miscalculation
of the Detection and/or Withdrawal Times.
34. The fact that the APR proceeded to the administration himself is a clear aggravating
circumstance, since, as an unauthorized person, the injection could have sustained
serious consequences to the Horse, if done incorrectly.
35. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the APR is not entitled to any reduction of the
otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
36. To the contrary, the Tribunal finds that the APR’s dangerous behaviour, amount to
aggravating factors which justify an increase of the Period of Ineligibility to be imposed
on the APR, of an overall seven (7) months, in accordance with Art. 10.4 of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
37. In view of the above considerations, the Tribunal finds that the applicable period of
Ineligibility is seven (7) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which shall
commence on the date of notification of this decision.
38. The Tribunal also deems that the APR shall pay a fine of CHF 5,000 and pay CHF 2’000 to
the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
VI. Terms of the Decision
39. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr ALDHUWAYHI violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.

b) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is suspended for a period of seven (7) months. The period of the
Ineligibility will be effective from the date of notification of this decision.
c) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is ordered to pay a fine of five thousand Swiss Francs (CHF 5,000).
d) Mr ALDHUWAYHI is ordered to pay two thousand Swiss francs (2’000 CHF) to the
FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
40. Mr ALDHUWAYHI, the Saudi NF and the FEI will be notified this Decision.
41. Mr ALDHUWAYHI may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any capacity in

Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is authorized or
organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any capacity in
Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level event
organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
42. If Mr ALDHUWAYHI violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph during the

43. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
44. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
